title: The tongue tip for /l/
goal: Practise /l/ and use it in a short, understandable exchange.
cue: Touch the ridge behind your upper teeth with your tongue tip. Let air pass around the sides. Final American l may sound darker than initial l; keep the tongue relaxed.
spelling: l often represents /l/. Final l belongs to the word; avoid adding another syllable.
task: Ask for a direction and repeat “left” clearly.
story: A leaf is on the table. Lily feels its soft edge.
reviewPrompt: Return to day 12, 19, 23, 25. Recall a word or say one useful phrase before opening those lessons.

articulation.label: lip
articulation.alt: lip: /l/ → /ɪ/ → /p/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /l/: Tip at the ridge; air passes round the sides.
/ɪ/: Front tongue, a little lower and relaxed.
/p/: Close the lips, then release the air.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.
